Abstract:Knowledge editing has emerged as a promising approach for efficiently updating embedded knowledge in large language models (LLMs). It first computes an ideal target hidden state that steers the LLM toward the new output, and then edits the model parameters so that the original hidden state is mapped to this target. While most existing methods focus on the second stage of parameter editing in preserving other knowledge, we find that the upstream construction of the target hidden state also plays an important role in allocating the model’s limited capacity space. We first establish a theoretical connection between interference in the parameter space and interference between target hidden states, showing that the two are positively correlated. Building on this insight, we propose a simple yet effective \ell_1 regularization method that prunes away unnecessary ``tentacles’’ of each knowledge vector, retaining only the essential components. With fewer extraneous tentacles, each edit affects less other knowledge, enabling better coexistence. Extensive experiments across multiple LLMs and benchmark datasets verify the effectiveness of our method. Code: this https URL.

[NLP-86] ZeroPoint: Lightweight Energy-Based Decision Model

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决能量模型（Energy-based Models, EBMs）在决策任务中无法有效处理“无选项可接受”这一情形的问题。传统EBM仅能学习选项间的相对兼容性，缺乏一个固定的能量参考点来判断是否存在可接受的选项，导致模型无法自主决定是否拒绝所有选项。其解决方案的关键在于提出一种名为ZeroPoint的新框架，将“不选择任何选项”作为模型的一个固定状态，且该状态在任意输入下能量恒为零。这一设定为所有选项提供了明确的能量参照系，使得选项的非负能量深度可直接反映其相对于“空答案”的兼容性。决策过程（选或不选）成为统一推理的一部分，通过负对数似然损失进行端到端训练，无需额外设计拒识规则。模型采用一个顺序无关的小型多语言编码器，联合读取输入与所有选项，实验表明，主要性能提升来源于包含“无合适选项”示例的训练数据，其在区分有/无可接受选项方面优于学习型拒识类和阈值softmax方法，同时保持选项间选择能力不变。

作者: Javier Marín
机构: 未知
类目: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL); Machine Learning (cs.LG)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Energy-based models (EBMs) assign a scalar energy to every joint value of the observed and predicted variables. In decision models, the prediction is chosen from a finite list of options provided with each input. Inference then reduces to comparing the energies of the options, and training lowers the energy of the correct option relative to the others. A complete decision must also account for the possibility that no option is acceptable. However, the energies learned by a standard EBM define only relative compatibility: adding the same input-dependent quantity to all energies leaves the predictions, the Gibbs distribution, and the usual training losses unchanged. The model therefore has no learned reference level against which to decide whether any option fits. We propose ZeroPoint, an EBM that makes the empty answer a state of the model with energy zero for every input. This fixed state provides an explicit reference for the energies of all listed options, whose non-negative depths measure their compatibility with the input relative to the empty answer. The options and the empty answer share one distribution, in which an option at zero depth receives no probability. The decision to select an option or to abstain is thus part of ordinary inference, trained with the negative log-likelihood loss, rather than a separate rejection rule. The energy function is a small multilingual encoder that reads the input together with all the options and is invariant to their order. Ablations show that most of the benefit comes from training with examples in which no option fits. With the same encoder and data, the fixed zero separates inputs with and without an acceptable option slightly better than a learned rejection class and clearly better than a thresholded softmax, while leaving the choice among options unchanged.

[NLP-87] racing Psychometric Inference in Large Language Models NEURIPS2026

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决生成式语言模型是否在内部表征心理构念（psychological constructs），抑或仅生成在表面上呈现心理测量结构的输出这一核心问题。其关键解决方案在于采用跨人格（cross-persona）范式，结合行为层面的跨量表相关性分析与内部表征的几何结构探测，系统检验模型在多尺度心理特征预测中的表现。研究发现，较大规模的指令微调（instruct）模型不仅在输出层面重现并放大人类被试间的跨量表相关性，且其内部激活空间的几何结构与人类心理矩阵存在显著对齐；而基础（base）模型则缺乏此类对齐。进一步通过匹配的激活探针（activation-probing）分析揭示，探针斜率与行为斜率之间存在“读出衰减”（readout attenuation）现象，即探针所捕捉的内部结构强度低于实际行为表现的放大程度。经由合成控制与可靠性代理校正后，调整后的探针斜率仍与行为放大效应显著相关（r = 0.88），表明内部结构具有可解码性与几何一致性。因此，该研究的关键突破在于通过多层级验证，证明了大模型在特定条件下具备对心理构念的内在表征能力，而非单纯模仿表面结构。

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.12937
作者: Chih-Hao Hsu,Feng-Chun B. Chou,Pin-Hao A. Chen
机构: National Taiwan University(台湾大学)
类目: Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Computation and Language (cs.CL)
备注: Accepted at NeurIPS 2026

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Do large language models represent psychological constructs internally, or do they only generate outputs that resemble psychometric structure? We address this question using a cross-persona paradigm across 14 model variants from two families (Llama 3 and Qwen 2.5, 0.5B-14B, base and instruct). Given responses on one psychological scale from real individuals (N = 272 Taiwanese university students), models predict responses on six other scales. At the behavioral level, larger variants reproduce and amplify human cross-scale correlations; amplification persists after correcting the seven-scale human correlations for measurement attenuation. We then examine whether this structure is reflected internally. Contrastive direction analysis finds geometry aligned with the human matrix in larger instruct variants, but little alignment in base variants under this assay. Across models, geometry strength is associated with behavioral amplification (r = 0.68, p = 0.008; partial r = 0.69 controlling for log size). To relate internal structure to output behavior, a matched activation-probing paradigm shows that probe slopes vary less than behavioral slopes (1.38-1.77 vs 0.52-1.53). A synthetic control shows that ridge probing can inflate these slopes; after subtracting a baseline based on a reliability proxy from another analysis, adjusted slopes remain associated with behavior (r = 0.88). We term the measured probe-behavior gap readout attenuation. These results establish decodability and geometric alignment under the tested assays, without showing that the measured directions mediate the cross-persona answers.

[NLP-88] Using LLM Agents to Evaluate Prosocial Interventions on Social Media Platforms

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决社交媒体平台在部署内容干预措施前缺乏系统性评估方法的问题，尤其针对如何有效提升用户对经认证新闻的接触与参与度这一关键挑战。其核心解决方案是基于OASIS框架构建了一种基于大语言模型（LLM-based）代理的仿真评估流程，通过生成13,835名具有独特个人特征的虚拟用户代理，在20个时间步内模拟其对真实世界推特（Twitter/X）内容的互动行为（如评论、点赞、转发、关注），从而系统性比较三种干预策略：增加新闻内容供给、提升内容优先级（upranking）、以及引入名人来源提示（celebrity source cues）。研究发现，所有干预均显著提升了新闻参与度，其中将新闻内容置于信息流显著位置的“上排”策略效果最为突出，且该效应在不同性别、年龄和教育水平的代理中均保持一致。进一步与人类受试者实验结果对比验证，显示仿真结果在方向性和剂量归一化效率上具有高度一致性。研究表明，基于大语言模型的代理仿真可作为平台干预措施在人力实验前的早期评估工具，且相较于单纯增加内容数量或强调来源身份，提升内容可见性（upranking）可能更具效能。

Abstract:Social media platforms are a primary source of information for many users. Although research explores various interventions to promote prosocial content or demote harmful content on platforms, there are few systematic methods for evaluating competing intervention designs before conducting costly human-subject experiments. We develop a simulation-based evaluation pipeline built on the OASIS framework. We generate 13,835 LLM-based agents, each with a unique profile. Over 20 time steps, we expose them to real-world Twitter/X posts and let them comment, like, repost, or follow. We use those agents to systematically evaluate three interventions that increase exposure to verified news: adding content, upranking content, and celebrity source cues. All interventions significantly increase news engagement, with upranking news to prominent feed positions producing the largest effects. These effects hold across agents’ gender, age, and education levels. We validate our injection treatment results against a comparable human-subject study and find strong directional alignment and similar dose-normalized efficiency. Our results suggest that LLM-based agent simulations can support early-stage evaluation of platform interventions before human-subject deployment, and upranking may be more effective than news volume or source.

[NLP-89] Möbius Interaction Filtering: Order-Selective Spectral Regularization for Multimodal Humor Detection

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决多模态幽默检测中如何有效融合语言、语音和视觉模态信息，并合理调控不同层次交互（如单模态、双模态、三模态）对最终判断的贡献问题。其核心挑战在于，高阶交互虽蕴含丰富语义，但易受噪声干扰，导致信号-噪声比下降，影响模型鲁棒性。解决方案的关键是提出莫比乌斯交互滤波（Möbius Interaction Filtering, MoIF），通过设计一种具有几何递减响应特性的交互阶次滤波机制，在保持高阶表示能力的同时，对不同阶次交互进行有序调控。具体而言，MoIF构建私有时序编码器与平衡互作用结构，实现对单模态、双模态及三模态预测器的监督学习，并通过其聚合结构施加顺序选择性谱正则化，使最终集成结果精确对应于莫比乌斯域中的滤波函数。实验表明，该方法在UR-FUNNY数据集上实现了70.6%的准确率与加权F1，较联合训练的三模态基线提升1.62–2.79倍的信噪比，且在扰动下仍保持稳定的类对齐信号；在CMU-MOSI与CMU-MOSEI上的扩展验证进一步证明其在情感预测任务中的普适性与稳定性。MoIF通过可执行的谱约束将多模态交互组织方式与统计可靠性相联系，为多模态融合提供了理论清晰且性能优越的新范式。

Abstract:Multimodal humor detection requires interpreting language, vocal delivery, and visual behavior jointly. Expressive fusion must also regulate how interactions of different orders enter the final judgment. We propose Möbius Interaction Filtering (MoIF), which learns a modality-subset prediction function and imposes order-selective spectral regularization through its aggregation structure. Private temporal encoders and balanced reciprocal interaction construct supervised unimodal, bimodal, and trimodal predictors. Their uniform aggregate is exactly a Möbius-domain filter with a geometrically decreasing interaction-order response. This formulation retains higher-order representations while regulating their contribution to prediction. Controlled UR-FUNNY perturbations reveal a pronounced decline in label-aligned signal-to-noise ratio across interaction orders. The induced filter improves the final ratio by 1.62-2.79 times relative to the co-trained trimodal predictor while preserving its own clean class-aligned signal under perturbation. Five-seed experiments achieve 70.6% accuracy and weighted F1 on UR-FUNNY, exceeding thirteen reproduced methods on these detection metrics. CMU-MOSI and CMU-MOSEI evaluations establish applicability to sentiment prediction, and cross-seed analyses show more stable estimates on all three datasets. MoIF connects the organization of multimodal interactions to their statistical reliability through an executable spectral constraint. Code is available at this https URL.

[NLP-90] Brasilidade: Measuring Brazilian Identity for Large Language Models

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决当前大语言模型（LLM）在评估巴西葡萄牙语（Brazilian Portuguese）语言能力时存在的局限性，特别是缺乏针对该语言特有语法、语义细微差别及方言变体的系统性评估基准。其解决方案的关键在于提出名为Brasilidade的新基准评估方法，该方法由标准化任务构成，覆盖四个不同领域，首次公开了涵盖语言细微差别、语法结构及巴西葡萄牙语变体的第一领域任务。实验结果表明，模型规模本身并不能决定性能表现，多个中等规模模型在特定评测协议中超越了更大模型；尽管部分模型专为葡萄牙语训练，但整体表现并未显著优于平均水平。此外，不同任务层级揭示了显著的语言复杂性：部分任务对多数模型而言较为简单，而另一些则构成极端挑战，还存在性能波动较大的混合型任务，凸显出现有模型在处理巴西葡萄牙语时的不均衡能力。因此，该研究强调构建专门针对巴西葡萄牙语语言特性与复杂性的评估基准的重要性，以推动未来训练周期有针对性地改进模型在该语言上的表现。

Abstract:This work presents a new benchmark that aims to address the limitations of current methods for evaluating LLMs in Brazilian Portuguese. We introduced Brasilidade, an assessment methodology comprised of standardized tasks distributed across four different domains, and we are making available the tasks from its first domain, which address nuances of the language, grammar, and variations of Brazilian Portuguese. The results show that model size, by itself, does not determine performance; several medium-sized models outperformed larger models in the protocols evaluated. Specific models for Portuguese, in general, did not perform above average, despite their targeted training. Different task levels revealed significant nuances: while some tasks proved easy for most models, others posed extreme challenges, and some yielded mixed results, with wide variations in performance. This clearly illustrates the need for benchmarks that address the limitations of the models in Brazilian Portuguese, allowing future training cycles to seek to overcome them. [NLP-91] Actionable Feedback: Improving Model Capabilities from User Edit Data on Clinical Documentation

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决在临床文档生成任务中，利用真实部署环境下医生对大语言模型（LLM）输出的编辑作为监督信号时所面临的“不可靠反馈”问题。具体而言，研究发现超过45%的编辑内容包含了未被原始输入支持的新增信息，若直接基于此类编辑进行微调，会加剧模型幻觉（hallucination）现象。其解决方案的关键在于：首先基于真实部署数据构建了一套医生编辑行为的分类体系（taxonomy of clinician-editing behaviors），进而基于该分类体系在MIMIC-III公开数据集上生成半合成的医生编辑数据；最后引入简单有效的过滤机制，通过专家评审验证，识别出具有可操作性的、与输入上下文一致的“有依据编辑”（grounded edits）。实证结果表明，相较于直接对原始编辑数据进行微调导致的幻觉增加，该渐进式过滤方法能在提升模型与临床医生偏好一致性的同时，有效保持生成内容对输入事实的忠实性（faithfulness）。

作者: Daniel P. Jeong,Yewon Byun,John Giorgi,Peng Xu,Zachary C. Lipton,Michael Oberst
机构: Carnegie Mellon University (卡内基梅隆大学); Abridge AI; Johns Hopkins University (约翰霍普金斯大学)
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Machine Learning (cs.LG)
备注: Preprint

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Large language models (LLMs) are increasingly being deployed in clinical documentation workflows, where clinicians review and edit their outputs before use. In principle, these clinician edits represent a scalable source of supervision for model training. In practice, not all edits represent actionable feedback: for instance, on data drawn from real-world deployment of an AI clinical documentation product, our review suggests that over 45% of edited outputs contain user-added information that is not directly supported by the inputs to the model. Naively fine-tuning on such edits risks teaching the model to hallucinate. In this paper, we develop a method to address this challenge. Given that real clinician edits on deployed documentation tools are not publicly available, we first develop a taxonomy of clinician-editing behaviors, informed by data from a deployed AI clinical documentation product. Then, we develop a method for generating semi-synthetic clinician-edit data, informed by our taxonomy, on a discharge-summary generation task based on MIMIC-III, a public dataset. Finally, we introduce simple filtering methods for identifying actionable edits, with accuracy evaluated by expert review. We show empirically, on our semi-synthetic dataset, that naive fine-tuning on raw edited output increases ungrounded content, while our approach of progressively filtering toward grounded edits enables improvement on clinician-alignment metrics while retaining faithfulness to the input context.

[NLP-92] SELD: Detecting Silent Evidence Loss in Context Compression beyond the Answer

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决长输入语言模型中上下文压缩（context compression）导致的“隐性证据丢失”（silent evidence loss）问题。其核心挑战在于：现有方法依赖于比较压缩前后模型的答案或最可能输出的词，无法识别关键证据已被移除但答案保持不变的情况，从而在后续模型复用该压缩上下文时引入潜在风险。本文提出无需训练和标签的检测方法SELD（Silent Evidence Loss Detector），其关键创新在于利用读者模型在未选择答案之间的偏好变化来捕捉证据损失——即使最终答案不变，若压缩导致支持性证据缺失，模型对其他候选答案的相对偏好仍会发生显著改变。通过构建SELD-Pairs基准数据集，涵盖来自三个问答数据集的长度匹配的证据删除与控制删除样本，实验表明，SELD在多种压缩器、压缩率及读者模型上均显著优于现有基线，在答案不变的情况下成功识别83%的证据删除实例，远超最强基线的70%，证明了即使在答案未变的情况下，也能有效检测到上下文压缩中的隐性证据丢失。

作者: Wentao Lei,Li Liu
机构: The Hong Kong University of Science and Technology (Guangzhou), China
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Context compression is now routine for language models with long inputs, but a compressed context is useful only if it keeps the evidence for the answer. Existing checks compare the reader model’s answer or its most likely words, and thus miss a frequent failure, silent evidence loss: key evidence is removed while the answer stays the same, leaving the answer unsupported and risky for other models that reuse the context. To address this challenge, we propose SELD (Silent Evidence Loss Detector), which needs no training and no labels. Its principle is that when evidence is lost, a reader model’s preferences among the answers it leaves unsaid shift even if its answer does not, so comparing these preferences before and after compression reveals losses that answer checks cannot see. We also build SEL-Pairs, a benchmark of length-matched evidence and control deletions from three question-answering datasets. Quantitative and qualitative experiments with five reader models on it show that SELD consistently outperforms strong and recent baselines across compressors, compression rates and models, identifying the evidence-removing edit in 83% of matched pairs with unchanged answers, against 70% for the strongest baseline. These results show that evidence loss in compressed contexts can be detected even when the answer is unchanged.

[NLP-93] meOmni-o1: Bidirectionally Coupling Time Series Foundation Models and LLM s for Multimodal Reasoning and Forecasting

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决多模态时间序列数据中联合理解与预测的难题，即如何在同时包含时间序列数值与相关文本描述（如事件报告）的场景下，实现对序列的语义理解（如问答）与未来值预测。现有方法存在明显局限：大语言模型（LLM）虽能处理文本并生成自然语言输出，但对长序列时间数据建模能力差；时间序列基础模型（TSFM）虽具备强大的预训练预测能力，却无法读取或生成文本；而现有融合架构往往仅单向利用预训练能力，未能充分发挥两者协同优势。本文提出TimeOmni-o1，其核心创新在于构建一个双向耦合的统一框架，将预训练的TSFM与LLM深度集成：一方面，TSFM以压缩形式编码时间序列供LLM进行联合推理；另一方面，LLM生成的语义推理结果被反馈至TSFM，用于条件化生成更精准的预测。该架构实现了跨模态读写（支持时间序列与文本的输入/输出）、联合推理与预训练能力复用。为训练该模型，研究构建了MMTR——一个涵盖12个领域的多模态时间序列推理数据集，包含超过50万条样本及标注的推理轨迹。实验表明，TimeOmni-o1在多项任务上显著优于现有模型，不仅超越单独使用的LLM与TSFM，还在多个公开基准测试中展现出领先性能。

作者: Ziyang Zhang,Shenyi Li,Wen Wu,Chao Zhang
机构: Tsinghua University (清华大学); Shanghai Artificial Intelligence Laboratory (上海人工智能实验室)
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL)
备注: Code: this https URL Project page: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Time series from real-world systems are often accompanied by text, such as a report on an event that affects them. Two common tasks on these series are understanding, e.g., answering questions about a series, and forecasting its future values. Both tasks require reasoning over the series and the text together. Moreover, understanding outputs text while forecasting outputs a time series, so serving both requires a model that reads and generates both modalities. Large language models (LLMs) read time series as digit tokens and handle long series poorly. Time series foundation models (TSFMs) forecast well from large-scale pretraining but typically neither read nor generate text. Time series language models add a time series modality to the LLM but forecast on the LLM side, leaving the TSFM’s pretrained forecasting ability unused. We present TimeOmni-o1, which couples a pretrained TSFM and an LLM bidirectionally. In one direction, the TSFM encodes the series in compressed form for the LLM, which reasons over it together with the text. In the other, the LLM’s reasoning is fed back into the TSFM, which produces the forecast conditioned on it. One model architecture thus reads and generates both series and text, reasons in text, and draws on the TSFM’s pretrained forecasting ability. To train it, we build MMTR, a multimodal time series reasoning dataset with annotated reasoning traces, covering both tasks across 12 domains with 500k+ samples. On MMTR, TimeOmni-o1 outperforms existing models on both understanding and forecasting across most domains, as well as the LLM and the TSFM inside it when used individually. The gains carry over to three open benchmarks, where it outperforms the dedicated time series models.

[NLP-94] Rethinking in Spikes: Mitigating Hallucinations in MDLMs with Step-Aware Decoding

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决多模态扩散语言模型（Multimodal Diffusion Language Models, MDLMs）在迭代去噪过程中出现的幻觉（hallucination）问题。研究表明，尽管整体去噪过程呈现熵值下降趋势，但部分去噪步骤中存在局部熵值突增，这些异常步骤与幻觉现象密切相关。为应对这一问题，论文提出一种名为StepRefine的即插即用解码策略，其核心在于基于熵值偏差检测异常步骤，并在此基础上实现“步感知”的离散去噪与潜在空间连续精炼之间的动态切换。具体而言，在熵值突增步骤中，模型采用概率加权嵌入以保留多样化的语义推理假设，进行多轮连续精炼；同时引入精炼控制器监控分布稳定性，避免冗余迭代并适时返回标准离散去噪流程。该方法通过保留掩码位置的分布信息，增强了候选语义与上下文间的持续交互，从而有效缓解幻觉，显著提升多模态基准上的生成可靠性。

作者: Zhongxing Xu,Zhonghua Wang,Zhe Qian,Shiyan Su,Ming Hu,Xiaocheng Zou,Wei Feng,Mingquan Lin,Yuyin Zhou,Yifan Peng,Hamid Rezatofighi,Zongyuan Ge
机构: Monash University (莫纳什大学); Cornell University (康奈尔大学); UC Santa Cruz (加州大学圣克鲁斯分校); Northeastern University (东北大学); University of Minnesota (明尼苏达大学)
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Recent advancements in multimodal diffusion language models (MDLMs) have exhibited strong global modeling capabilities through iterative refinement. We observe that mask uncertainty follows an overall downward trend during iterative denoising, while a few denoising steps exhibit localized entropy spikes closely associated with hallucinations. We argue that anomalous steps can be identified by measuring the entropy deviation of each denoising step from its neighboring temporal window. We hypothesize that discrete token commitment discards the distributional information at masked positions, limiting the continued interaction between candidate semantics and the context during entropy spikes. With this goal, we present StepRefine, a plug-and-play decoding strategy that leverages semantic context to achieve reliable denoising. The core of our method lies in a step-aware switch between discrete denoising and latent refinement. The model employs probability-weighted embeddings at entropy spike steps to preserve diverse reasoning hypotheses and performs multiple rounds of continuous refinement. Meanwhile, a refinement controller monitors distributional stability to reduce unnecessary loops and switch the model back to standard discrete denoising. Through extensive experiments, StepRefine demonstrates significant hallucination mitigation across different MDLMs on multimodal benchmarks.

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决基于纵向社交媒体数据推断抑郁症量表（如贝克抑郁量表，BDI）响应时，如何有效提取可归因于个体且语义上与特定症状相关的证据问题。现有方法依赖语义相似性检索帖子，易引入误导性或非个人化的信息，尤其在多症状共现或讨论他人经历的文本中表现不佳。其解决方案的关键在于提出SREE（Symptom Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded InfErence）框架：通过识别第一人称、症状特异性的文本片段，采用受设施选址（Facility Location）启发的目标选择代表性证据子集，并基于所选证据进行证据门控推理（Evidence-Gated Inference）。该方法显著提升了证据检索的精确率（相对提升70%）和F1值（相对提升59%），同时减少至少30%的冗余帖子；在多症状句子场景下，即使使用双倍检索预算仍优于密集检索模型。在eRisk 2019–2021三个数据集上的实验表明，SREE在项目级精确匹配率上达到最优，且在序数和聚合指标上保持竞争力，验证了局部化可归因证据并控制其组成对准确推断抑郁症量表响应的重要性。

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Longitudinal social-media histories offer an opportunity to assess depression, potentially supporting the inference of standardized depression questionnaire responses. However, this task requires evidence that is semantically relevant to a symptom and attributable to the user, while being sufficiently specific to support an individual questionnaire item. Existing approaches rely on semantic similarity to retrieve posts, which can introduce misleading or non-attributable evidence, particularly in multi-symptom posts and discussions of others’ experiences. We propose SREE (Symptom Retrieval and Evidence-Grounded InfErence), an evidence-grounded pipeline that extracts first-person and symptom-specific text spans, selects a representative subset using a Facility Location-inspired objective, and performs Evidence-Gated Inference over the selected evidence. We evaluate evidence retrieval on BDI-Sen and evidence-conditioned questionnaire inference on eRisk 2019-2021. Compared with state-of-the-art retrieval approaches, SREE achieves relative improvements of 70% in post-level precision and 59% in F1, while retaining at least 30% fewer posts. On multi-symptom sentences, it also outperforms dense retrieval in precision and F1 even with twice the retrieval budget. Across all three eRisk collections, SREE achieves the highest exact item-level agreement while remaining competitive on ordinal and aggregate metrics. These results highlight the importance of localizing attributable evidence and controlling its composition before inferring depression questionnaire responses.

[NLP-96] hermodynamics of words

【速读】： 该论文试图解决的问题是：如何从物理热化理论的角度解释文学作品中词汇频率分布的统计规律，特别是揭示罕见词大量出现且高频词集中于极低能量状态的现象。其解决方案的关键在于提出“词汇热化假说”（word thermalization hypothesis），将文本中的不同词汇类比为经典振子（或粒子），其词频（或相关标记数）对应于能量态上的占据因子。在此框架下，系统遵循总能量（即总词数）与总概率归一化（即不同词汇数量）守恒原则，从而模拟出类似于瑞利-金斯（Rayleigh-Jeans, RJ）热化与凝聚的统计行为。研究发现，实际文学文本中的有效系统能量极低，导致显著的RJ凝聚现象——即大量概率集中在最低能量态，对应于仅出现一次或两次的稀有词汇。该理论成功描述了16部文学作品（包括《圣经》、莎士比亚全集及美国国家语料库数据）中词频分布的幂律特征，并与洛伦兹曲线、帕累托曲线和齐普夫定律等经济与复杂系统中的经典模型高度吻合，揭示了语言系统与经济财富分布之间的深层相似性。

作者: Klaus M. Frahm,Dima L. Shepelyansky

点击查看摘要

Abstract:We introduce the word thermalization hypothesis according to which in a literary work there are effective interactions between words that drive them to thermalization where their word frequency distribution is the same as for the phenomenon of Rayleigh-Jeans (RJ) thermalization and condensation. In this concept, the different words play a role of classical oscillators (particles) and their word frequencies, or related tokens, are analogous to certain filling factors over energy state levels. The thermalization process is characterized by the conservation of total system energy, or total number of words/tokens, and total probability norm, or total number of different words. We apply this approach to analyze 16 literary works, including Bible, complete works of Shakespeare, and data from American National Corpus. We show that for these cases the effective system energy is very low and thus there is the RJ condensation phenomenon with a big fraction of total probability concentrated at the lowest energy states corresponding to a big fraction of rare words appearing only once or twice in the whole text. Such a RJ condensation is observed for light propagation in multimode optical fibers and other physical systems. We relate the thermalization of words to the recently proposed wealth thermalization for households in world countries. The economy concepts of Lorenz and Pareto curves, and also Zipf curves, are applied to the word frequency distributions of the selected 16 cases and it is shown that the thermalization theory gives a strikingly good description of real data.

[NLP-97] Walrus Technical Report

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决多任务、多语言、多说话人及混合语码（code-switching）场景下语音与音频理解与生成的统一建模难题，尤其针对现有模型在跨任务泛化能力、数据分布不均衡以及核心技能遗忘等方面存在的局限。其解决方案的关键在于提出一种以数据为中心的三阶段训练课程（data curriculum）策略，而非依赖新型网络架构；通过在标准解码器仅有的骨干网络（decoder-only backbone）上，基于Gemma 4初始化，并系统性地引入任务感知与数据集感知的加权机制，有效平衡不同任务间差异巨大的词元预算（token budget），同时防止在增量训练中对已有核心能力造成遗忘。该方法在超过6亿样本、涵盖100种语言和20余项任务的数据集上进行训练，使模型在多语言、多说话人及语码转换的自动语音识别（ASR）、语音翻译、情感识别、音频描述生成等任务上均取得领先性能，甚至在多数基准测试中超越了规模为其四倍的Qwen3-Omni模型。研究结果表明，高质量的数据工程是推动多任务语音与音频建模性能提升的核心驱动力。

Abstract:We present Walrus, a unified 8B speech-and-audio foundation model handling speech recognition (including code-switching and multi-talker speech), speech-to-text and speech-to-speech translation, text-to-speech, emotion recognition, audio captioning, and general audio understanding. Our main contribution is not a new architecture but a data-centric training recipe; we use a standard decoder-only backbone initialized from Gemma 4, so that gains can be traced to the data. For speech generation, Walrus predicts low-bitrate discrete speech tokens, and a lightweight token-to-waveform decoder converts them into high-fidelity audio. The recipe is a three-stage data curriculum that moves from broad multilingual data to multi-talker, code-switching, and domain-specific data. At each stage, task-aware and dataset-aware weighting balances tasks with very different token budgets and protects core skills from forgetting. Trained on over 600M samples covering more than 20 tasks and 100 languages, Walrus leads on most multilingual, multi-talker, and code-switching ASR, speech translation, and audio understanding benchmarks, outperforming both open speech language models of comparable size and dedicated task-specific models. On most benchmarks, it even matches or surpasses the 4\times larger Qwen3-Omni’s performance. Results suggest that data engineering is a primary driver of quality in multi-task speech and audio modeling.

[NLP-98] Off-target posterior mass: A training-free diagnostic for fine-tuning spoken language diarization probes

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决语音语言分割（Spoken Language Diarization, SLD）模型在不同数据集上进行预训练语音模型微调时，难以预测其性能提升幅度的问题。现有研究表明，微调对SLD性能的增益具有显著的数据集依赖性，但缺乏有效的指标来提前评估微调是否带来收益。为此，论文提出了一种名为“非目标后验质量”（Off-target Posterior Mass, OTPM）的诊断指标，该指标基于语言识别的后验概率计算，用于量化模型在非目标语言上的置信度分布。OTPM与微调后的性能增益呈现正相关关系，在未见过的合成双语数据上相关系数达0.56，在真实世界语料库中为0.23，表明OTPM具备作为SLD微调有效性预测工具的潜力。其关键在于利用后验概率分布特性构建可解释、可量化的诊断指标，从而实现对微调收益的早期评估，提升模型优化效率。

Abstract:Spoken Language Diarization (SLD) models provide frame-level language information of a speech recording. SLD modeling pipeline includes feature extraction from pre-trained speech models followed by clustering. Fine-tuning pre-trained speech models has shown performance gains for SLD with its magnitude being dataset dependent. Off-target Posterior Mass (OTPM), computed based on posterior language identification probabilities is proposed as a diagnostic metric to forecast performance gains from SLD fine-tuning. OTPM obtains positive correlation with probe gains, 0.56 on unseen synthetic bilingual data and 0.23 on real-world corpora. These results indicate promising potential of OTPM as a diagnostic metric for SLD.

[NLP-99] Orthographic depth at two scales with English also matched for lexicon size

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决读者在单一语言中阅读困难的问题，特别是探究拼写与发音映射的可预测性（predictability）对阅读能力的影响。其核心问题是：不同字母文字系统中，拼写到发音的映射不确定性（以条件熵衡量）如何影响阅读流畅性。解决方案的关键在于采用条件熵作为量化指标，从两个粒度层次（即音素对齐单元和音节）分析十二种字母正字法的拼写-发音映射不确定性。研究发现，英语在两种粒度下均表现出最高的不确定性，而芬兰语最低；葡萄牙语和丹麦语在对齐单元层面的不确定性高于英语，德语和意大利语则因粒度和转写方式不同而排序变化。此外，研究揭示了单位尺度扩大时不确定性趋势不一致——部分语言如西班牙语下降，德国语波动，芬兰语稳定，意大利语依赖转写方式，英语依赖词表，而挪威语和瑞典语则上升。尽管单词级总不确定性普遍下降，但该指标受发音边界设定和样本内记忆效应干扰，无法反映读者实际认知计算过程。通过严格匹配词典规模的20,000词样本验证，发现音节尺度的熵与初学者阅读准确率呈显著负相关（ρ = -0.74），表明音节层级的拼写-发音可预测性可能是影响阅读习得的重要因素。总体而言，该研究通过跨语言比较揭示了正字法结构中的可预测性差异，为理解阅读障碍的潜在成因提供了量化依据。

备注: 38 pages, 5 figures. Spelling-to-sound entropy as a measure of orthographic depth for cross-language reading research; exploratory check against Grade 1 reading accuracy in Section 3.5. Code and data: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:A reader can struggle to read in only one of their languages, and one proposed reason is how predictably spelling maps to sound. We measure that predictability as conditional entropy, the pronunciation uncertainty left once the spelling is seen, at two grain sizes (unit sizes): the alignment unit, an aligned spelling-sound chunk, and the syllable, bounded in the pronunciation. We analyse word lists in twelve alphabetic orthographies and report five in full, with English pronunciations from a dictionary and the rest from the synthesizer eSpeak-ng, length marks removed. Among the five, English has the most uncertainty and Finnish the least at both grains. Across all twelve, Portuguese and Danish exceed English per alignment unit, and German and Italian order differently by grain and transcription. These orders hold when English is transcribed by eSpeak-ng with u allowed to spell /j/ plus a vowel. Uncertainty per unit has no shared direction as units grow: it falls in Spanish and, less securely, German, is level in Finnish, depends on transcription in Italian and on the word list in English, and rises in Norwegian and Swedish. Summed uncertainty per word falls in all twelve, but that score is handed the pronunciation’s boundaries and mixes context with in-sample memorisation, so it is no evidence of what a reader computes. An exact identity states when discarded spelling boundaries could reverse that fall. A uniform 20,000-word English sample holds 35% of the dictionary’s syllable spellings and has syllable entropy 0.098 bits lower, so lexicons must be matched in size. In an exploratory check over eleven languages, syllable-scale entropy tracked first-year reading accuracy (rho = -0.74, falling to -0.25 if English is given the lowest entropy instead), without separating the syllable scale from the alignment unit. These estimates describe sampled writing systems, not readers.

【速读】： 该论文旨在解决医疗领域机器学习分类器训练中普遍存在的数据稀缺问题。由于伦理顾虑和数据隐私限制，医学类研究的样本量通常远低于非医疗领域的数据集规模。为应对这一挑战，论文提出利用生成式模型进行数据增强，以提升在稀疏数据场景下分类器的鲁棒性。其解决方案的关键在于采用变分自编码器（Variational Autoencoder, VAE）等生成模型，对基于语音与音频特征的交互数据进行合成，从而扩充训练样本。实验表明，该方法显著提升了深度神经网络（DNN）分类器的性能：在区分记忆门诊中四类典型患者群体的任务中，F-score由58%提升至约74%，实现了16%的性能改进。

Abstract:Data limitation is one of the most common issues in training machine learning classifiers for medical applications. Due to ethical concerns and data privacy, the number of people that can be recruited to such experiments is generally smaller than the number of participants contributing to non-healthcare datasets. Recent research showed that generative models can be used as an effective approach for data augmentation, which can ultimately help to train more robust classifiers sparse data domains. A number of studies proved that this data augmentation technique works for image and audio data sets. In this paper, we investigate the application of a similar approach to different types of speech and audio-based features extracted from interactions recorded with our automatic dementia detection system. Using two generative models we show how the generated synthesized samples can improve the performance of a DNN based classifier. The variational autoencoder increased the F-score of a four-way classifier distinguishing the typical patient groups seen in memory clinics from 58% to around 74%, a 16% improvement

作者: Arjun Rao,Nishant Gopinath
类目: Information Retrieval (cs.IR); Computation and Language (cs.CL)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Text-to-SQL systems over large pooled catalogs must first retrieve the tables a question needs. We compare against the published table recall of RASL, which uses Claude 3.5 models to extract keywords and select tables, on pooled BIRD, Spider, and Fiben catalogs. FERN (Feature-Engineered Ranking with No generative LLM) instead fuses three frozen retrievers into 100 candidates, describes each with up to 120 features, and reorders them with LightGBM rankers fitted once on BIRD’s training questions. On Spider, where it was not fitted, its candidate pool alone reaches RASL’s published recall at fifteen tables (98.0), and the ranker raises the share of questions with every gold table in the top five (complete@5) from 83.9% to 95.6%. At five tables, FERN’s recall is within one point of RASL’s on Spider (96.7 vs 97.0) and on BIRD with its evidence hints (96.6 vs 97.5), and 8.2 points below on BIRD without them (89.3). On 121 real BEAVER questions, without BEAVER fitting, its recall at fifteen (82.1) falls between two BEAVER-trained retrievers (80.8, 84.5), but its complete@15 is below both (49.6 vs 54.5 and 62.0). On Fiben, it falls far short at fifteen tables (54.2 vs 69.2, different question sets), although its recall at fifty is numerically close to RASL’s question-only retrieval result (80.7 vs 79.4). On BIRD dev with evidence, non-retrieval features raise complete@5 by 7.7 points over retrieval signals alone. On BIRD dev, median latency is 208 ms per question on one A100, without hosted model calls.

[IR-1] Point-in-Time Encoders for Earnings Calls

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14325
作者: Alessio Brini
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL); Information Retrieval (cs.IR); Statistical Finance (q-fin.ST)
备注: 10 pages, 3 figures, 7 tables. Accepted at the 3rd IEEE International Workshop on Large Language Models for Finance, IEEE BigData 2026. Code: this https URL

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Text encoders turn earnings calls into vectors for search, for language models that answer from retrieved passages, and for forecasting models. A live retriever can use an encoder trained once on all available text, as finance retrievers are, but a backtest needs an encoder that read no text written after the date of each vector. To address this look-ahead bias, from 412,248 calls we train vintages under four pretraining recipes, with yearly cutoffs from 2010 to 2024, and each vintage reads only text dated on or before its cutoff. We then fine-tune each vintage on the question-answer pairs of the calls themselves. The vintages we train on calls alone, with 33.8M parameters, retrieve answers on held-out calls better than the general retrievers we tested in every test quarter. Their vectors also raise by about half the rank correlation between next-day returns and forecasts built from past returns and firm size. When each vintage continues the previous one, a later vintage retrieves better on earlier quarters than the vintage available at the time, and a point-in-time language model that answers from the passages the later vintage retrieves inherits the gain. The 2024 vintage of our families also forecasts earnings surprises better, although the interval of this gain includes zero on calls that no vintage read. It forecasts returns no better, so point-in-time vintages matter most for retrieval and little for forecasts of returns.

作者: Boris Malashenko,Ivan Jarsky,Egor Soldatov,Vladislav Luzhnov,Sviatoslav Stumpf,Vladislav Shmatkov,Viacheslav Shalamov,Andrey Stankevich,Valeria Efimova
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL); Information Retrieval (cs.IR)

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Transformer sentence encoders provide strong retrieval quality, but their inference cost becomes a bottleneck when embeddings must be produced on CPUs or refreshed frequently. We introduce StaRSE, a compact Russian static sentence encoder that removes Transformer inference at deployment time: token directions are stored as sign bits, token norms are stored separately, and sentences are encoded by mean pooling over norm-scaled sign directions. StaRSE is initialized from ruBERT-base, fine-tuned on Russian adjacent-sentence and task-shaped pairs, and post-trained with a contrastive stage that directly optimizes the sign-projected token table. On RuMTEB, StaRSE reaches a task mean of 51.16 , 7.98 points above the strongest included static baseline. The packaged model occupies 11.3 MiB and has a mean CPU latency of 0.08 ms per sentence, compared with an estimated 55.7 MiB 16-bit parameter footprint and 1.43 ms mean CPU latency for the closest-quality contextual encoder. Ablations examine adjacent-sentence supervision, token norms, and direct sign-projected post-training.

[IR-3] SHARP: Semantic Hierarchical Agent ic Reasoning for Next POI Prediction with Dynamic Memory

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14220
作者: Yuhang Zhan,Silin Zhou,Zhuo Chen,Haoxiang Lei,Yunren Feng,Lisi Chen,Shuo Shang
类目: Information Retrieval (cs.IR)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Next point-of-interest (POI) prediction supports personalized location services by anticipating users’ next destinations. Recent methods leverage large language models (LLMs) for semantic reasoning and graphs for collective mobility modeling, improving POI prediction. However, three challenges still remain. Bridging LLMs’ semantic reasoning and specific POI prediction remains challenging. User mobility also evolves over time, making it necessary to retain and update historical knowledge within limited LLM contexts. Meanwhile, global transition graphs smooth out time-specific category transition patterns. To address these challenges, we propose Semantic Hierarchical Agentic Reasoning for Next POI Prediction with Dynamic Memory (SHARP), an agentic hierarchical framework in which category-level reasoning guides specific POI prediction. A trajectory memory agent maintains a dynamic trajectory memory bank that preserves earlier mobility patterns and tracks behavioral changes with limited context growth. We construct multi-granularity time-aware category transition graphs with global and time-conditioned views to preserve temporal regularities obscured by global aggregation. A category predict agent combines these graphs with trajectory memory to predict likely next categories. SHARP learns semantic IDs (SIDs) through a residual-quantized variational autoencoder (RQ-VAE) to construct semantic POI representations, which are jointly optimized with a category-guided POI predictor end-to-end. On three real-world datasets, SHARP improves Acc@5 and Acc@10 by an average of 5.29 and 4.52 percentage points, respectively, over the strongest baseline.

[IR-4] From Search to Decision: How Post-Training Shapes Information-Seeking Capabilities in Large Language Models

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14149
作者: Haohang Huang,Xuan Lu,Mingjin Kuai,Yuxuan Zhang,Wei Ji,Haiyang Zhang
类目: Information Retrieval (cs.IR)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Information seeking in large language model (LLM) systems increasingly involves decisions about when to acquire information, where to search, and how to evaluate and use evidence. Recent post-training methods have improved several such behaviors, but their objectives and evaluations span different tasks and system settings. This paper organizes research around six interrelated information-seeking capabilities and examines the learning signals, optimization methods, update loci, and credit-assignment mechanisms used to develop them. We synthesize empirical progress in targeted behaviors, end-to-end performance, search control, and generalization. Existing studies report gains in retrieval routing, query refinement, multi-tool exploration, evidence-grounded reasoning, and resource-aware search, although the scope of behavioral evidence varies across capabilities. We identify open challenges in estimating prospective retrieval utility, coordinating information-seeking decisions, and adapting to unfamiliar retrieval environments, and discuss evaluation practices for interpreting future progress.

Abstract:Retrieving evidence from Indian Knowledge Systems is complicated by transliteration variants, ambiguous names, and relations distributed across passages. We present an ontology-guided knowledge graph (KG) pipeline that links typed entities and relations extracted with Qwen3-32B to original textual evidence. We evaluate KG alone, single-vector retrieval (SV), and KG unions with SV and Entity Notes on 320 questions from Dhara Bench, matching the per-question candidate count across internal systems under BGE and Qwen rerankers. Standalone KG has the highest Precision@5 under both rerankers and the highest MRR@20 in Counting, Composite, and Multi-hop among the evaluated internal configurations. With Qwen, KG achieves Multi-hop MRR@20 of 0.8722, compared with 0.7622 for the fully reranked KG + SV union. The KG + SV + Entity Notes union instead provides the highest overall Recall@20 (0.5134), compared with 0.4347 for KG. On the 15 Multi-hop questions, Qwen KG achieves complete-evidence MRR@20 of 0.4651 versus 0.3372 for SV, while both full unions complete ten questions within twenty results compared with nine for KG. Gemini 3.7 Flash, evaluated through manually reviewed source mappings, re mains stronger on overall MRR and nDCG, while internal systems have category-specific advantages. All comparisons are descriptive. A separate deployment timing study measures mean retrieval times of 20.374 s for KG and 0.646 s for SV. The findings support selecting KG or its unions according to the required balance of early relevance, evidence completeness, and retrieval cost.

Abstract:Many heritage institutions hold extensive collections of show programs. Too numerous to be cataloged individually, they remain difficult to access and are still largely undigitized. This paper presents a workflow for transforming such documents into structured, interoperable data by combining vision-language models (VLMs), a custom extension of the Linked Art ontology for the performing arts, and different approaches for automatic semantic data annotation. Using the Festival d’Avignon programs (1947–present), preserved at the Bibliothèque nationale de France, as a case study, we demonstrate how VLMs achieve more than 98% text transcription accuracy from heterogeneous heritage document images and how constraining large language model generation through a knowledge graph significantly reduces hallucinations in semantic annotation. We argue that this workflow opens new possibilities for large-scale, interoperable performing arts historiography, including the creation of catalogues raisonnés for performing artists, a form of scholarship common in visual arts but absent in performing arts studies.

Abstract:As multimodal tourism-related information collected from heterogeneous data sources has become increasingly available, learning effective representations has attracted attention for improving recommendation performance. Existing approaches often tightly couple multimodal fusion with the architecture and optimization objective of a specific downstream model, which limits the generality and reusability of the learned representations. To address these limitations, we propose LUMIR, a decoupled multimodal representation learning framework based on contrastive learning. Multimodal information collected from heterogeneous data sources is first semantically unified into a shared textual representation space using large language models (LLMs). To evaluate the learned representations, experiments are conducted on a multimodal point-of-interest (POI) dataset under the next-POI recommendation setting across multiple sequential recommendation backbones. The results show that LUMIR consistently outperforms existing multimodal fusion baselines in both accuracy-oriented and beyond-accuracy metrics, demonstrating that decoupling representation learning from downstream optimization provides an effective paradigm for learning reusable multimodal representations. Abstract:Modern recommender systems increasingly consider diverse data modalities to enhance model performance. Focusing on tourism recommendation, we examine real-world challenges encountered when using datasets from Yelp and Instagram. Issues include noise from fake reviews, hallucinated content from LLMs, modality contradictions, and demographic bias. Abstract:Taxonomies are structured knowledge representations that support semantic search, recommendation, product catalog organization, and retrieval-augmented generation. Their automated construction from a fixed set of candidate entities requires more than plausible text generation: the resulting hierarchy must be complete, structurally valid, and semantically coherent. Large Language Models (LLMs) are promising for this task, but iterative free-form generation remains vulnerable to omitted or hallucinated entities, invalid hierarchical relations, and inconsistent organizational principles. We introduce TIGA (Taxonomy Induction with Tool-Grounded Agents), a knowledge-engineering architecture that formulates taxonomy induction as an iterative decision process over an explicit state and constrained action space. TIGA combines executable taxonomy-editing tools, an memory that records tool calls, rationales, and outcomes, and a runtime-adaptive organizational policy that the agent revises during inference. An optional global reviewer evaluates the constructed taxonomy against the candidate set and the active policy. We evaluate TIGA on four benchmark taxonomies using two LLM backbones and compare it with single-shot and iterative prompting-based baselines. TIGA achieves the strongest structural-quality results in most evaluated configurations, but does not dominate on every precision measure. The gains are accompanied by substantially higher token consumption, API-call volume, and inference time. Ablation results show consistent benefits from the policy and interaction-memory components, whereas the effect of global review depends on the dataset and the available revision budget. These findings characterize tool grounding and runtime policy adaptation as promising but costly mechanisms for improving the controlled construction of structured knowledge representations.

Abstract:Recommender systems increasingly influence what users discover and consume online, yet the decision logic behind their outputs often remains opaque. Counterfactual explanation (CFX) methods provide an effective way to show which changes to a user’s interaction history would alter a recommendation. In recommendation settings, however, CFXs often require many edits, producing long, low-level lists that are hard for users to interpret. Moreover, most evaluations emphasize edit counts while largely overlooking whether the resulting CFXs are coherent and actionable for users. We argue that this gap between generating valid CFXs and communicating model behavior stems from the lack of user-centered abstraction and limited qualitative evaluation. To bridge this gap, we investigate large language models as mediators that summarize raw CFX interaction edit lists into concise natural language explanations describing higher-level preference patterns. We optimize these mediators for correctness, informativeness, and linguistic quality through preference optimization, and evaluate the resulting explanations with human-calibrated metrics derived from separate human-labeled datasets. On the MovieLens-1M dataset, across multiple counterfactual generators and language models, the resulting summaries achieve high overall linguistic quality, while the strongest semantic results are obtained with high-success CFX methods such as ACCENT and SPINRec. Direct Preference Optimization improves the semantic metrics in almost all evaluated settings.

Abstract:Verifying corporate financial disclosures against the International Financial Reporting Standards (IFRS) is a core auditing task in which experts cross-reference disclosures with hundreds of fine-grained regulatory paragraphs: a laborious, costly, and error-prone process that motivates growing interest in large language models (LLMs) as compliance assistants. On the disagreement set, the ensemble achieves 81.7% weighted F1, exceeding the strongest single LLM by 10.4 points and majority voting by 14.6 points, and outperforms eleven unsupervised aggregation baselines; the retrieval pipeline attains Recall@15 of 45.3% on unseen regulations. Abstract:Researchers and engineers improve recommendation systems by performing A/B experiments with new model architectures, optimization methods, and data features. However, running full-scale experiments (e.g., full-model training with online data) for every feature change is prohibitively computationally intensive, while the result from a single small-scale experiment is often misleading. To address this challenge, we show that modern recommendation models exhibit feature-invariant scaling: the change of a model’s performance follows a predictable scaling-law even when different feature changes are applied to the baseline model. We introduce an efficient method that exploits scaling-laws and uses statistical inference to predict (with confidence intervals) the full-scale effect of an A/B experiment in recommendation systems. This enables practitioners to efficiently filter out neutral or regressive feature changes with only small-scale experimentation. We validate our method on three distinct recommendation model families—Wukong, HSTU, and LLM-based recommendation models—across more than 40 architectural, optimization, and data changes. Our method accurately distinguishes beneficial feature changes from neutral and regressive ones while using only a fraction of the compute required for full-scale evaluation. It also identifies several changes that improve HSTU’s state-of-the-art performance on MovieLens-20M. Our results demonstrate that scaling laws can be practically exploited to make compute-efficient decisions for improving industrial-scale recommendation systems.

Abstract:Retrieval-augmented language model systems generally select context by query-conditioned relevance. We argue that long-lived AI systems require a second operator: activation-conditioned memory availability. We specify an architecture in which request and goal cues seed an authorized memory graph, activation and fan attenuation allocate a bounded traversal frontier, retrieved entities recursively emit cues, and a typed evidence graph is reconstructed before generation. The specification yields five architectural consequences about candidate selection, traversal control, graph regularization, evidence reconstruction, and reinforcement. We derive implementation-level cost estimates and define ablations, failure conditions, and a reproducible evaluation protocol. The central claim is narrowed or falsified if a simpler graph reranker matches full traversal on causal and temporal recovery under equal budgets. This architecture-and-analysis preprint reports no benchmark measurements. If the claim holds, retrieval returns the evidence path that makes a memory available, not only a ranked list.

Abstract:Banks now train foundation models on ordered sequences of customer events such as transactions, app sessions, and authorizations. An audit of 59 public dataset families retains five datasets; the most common defect is the lack of a calendar timestamp that orders events. No date lies within the time span of all five datasets, so each is split at its own cutoff, chosen by one rule fixed before any model is evaluated. In reference results the cell determines the best model: a transformer leads on seen items after the cutoff but scores zero on new items, a variant that embeds item metadata helps mainly on MicroLens, and repeating the user’s last item leads on new items in four of five datasets. This parameter-free control also shows that on three datasets most of the score lost after the cutoff reflects changed behavior rather than the model. The pipeline, the cutoff rule, and the per-cell user counts are publicly available.

Abstract:A document preserves the visible result of professional work but often discards the research, calculations, assumptions, evidence, and authorization boundaries behind it. Abstract:VLM-based agents solve complex tasks by iteratively interacting with environments, and their effectiveness depends heavily on how the environment exposes information and provides tools for acting on it. Abstract:Offline web-behavior benchmarks frequently insert the demonstrated action into a finite candidate set and then measure reranking. Abstract:We present MANA (Multi-perspective Alignment of NPC Agents), an interactive approach for authoring NPC behavior through embodied demonstration. We show MANA in the context of Minecraft, where a developer aligns NPCs while playing the game itself. Activating MANA lets the developer dynamically switch into the point of view (POV) of any character and demonstrate, in-situ, how it would act given the surrounding context, through both movement and dialogue. MANA then distills each demonstration into a generalized policy that maps in-game context to actions. Finally, once the developer switches to another NPC or exits MANA mode, this generalized policy drives the NPC on its own. We demonstrate MANA by aligning two initially generic Minecraft NPCs: Fletcher and Farmer to act aggressively and cowardly, respectively. After roughly 2 minutes of in-game play, each character exhibits consistent and believable behaviors across new, unseen scenarios.

Abstract:Two-dimensional haptic displays, such as programmable pin arrays and vibrotactile or friction-modulating touchscreens, enable tactile communication of complex shapes in a low-profile form factor. However, many shapes of interest, including CAD models, three-dimensional graphs, and map topographies, are inherently three-dimensional. This work investigates two methods for encoding 3-D information using a 2-D tactile display: (1) a single tactile height map providing coarse but quantifiable depth cues, and (2) a series of binary layers communicating sequential slices of a 3-D model, supporting more complex geometries such as overhangs and cavities. We further compare performance across two display types–a friction-modulating display and a pin array–to examine how the level of haptic abstraction affects users’ ability to decode discrete 3-D information. A user study demonstrates that participants were able to effectively complete a 3-D assembly task using both strategies, achieving high accuracy across all display types. While the pin array supported faster task completion and higher-rated–though not statistically significant–user experience than the friction-modulating display for the binary-layer task, these differences did not translate to significant differences in overall usability (i.e., reassembly accuracy success). Together, these results identify design trade-offs and inform development of future surface haptic displays that support the communication and interpretation of discrete 3-D information in tactile graphics.

Abstract:Users often complain that AI assistants such as ChatGPT are getting worse. Some versions do change, but human evaluation leaves a second possibility untested: the people judging may change. We separate the two on Chatbot Arena, a public platform where people compare answers from two anonymous large language models (LLMs) and pick the better one or say both are bad. We study 1,260,967 blind votes cast from May 2023 to August 2024 on pairs of models whose versions are fixed: dated vendor snapshots and models with fixed open weights. For the same pair of unchanged models, the share of votes saying “both are bad” rises by 1.71 percentage points a month on a mean of 17.1%, and by 1.91 points a month in 2024. In fourteen pairs observed often in both 2023 and 2024, it rose in every one, from 15.5% to 23.3%. The ranking does not trend: in 2024, the stronger model’s share of decisive votes is flat. The rise holds within the same voter and on the same pair, and across arrival cohorts from their first recorded vote. It holds with prompt controls, in every major language, for dated vendor snapshots, open-weight models and models with stable answer length, and between interface changes. The drift is shared across models: month effects estimated from other models’ pairs remove it from each model’s own pairs. Platform-wide, the average model would be expected to score 78% against the 2023 average, yet the share of “both are bad” votes ended near where it began. The pattern fits a standard that follows the category’s progress, so a product that stands still is judged as declining. Absolute verdicts on AI drifted while relative comparisons held steady, an evaluation drift that matters for LLM leaderboards and for the human feedback used to train models.

Abstract:Ambient artificial intelligence (AI) scribes have moved rapidly from experimental pilots to enterprise-wide deployment across health systems, promising reduced documentation burden and improved clinician experience. While research evaluating these tools has expanded quickly, there are no agreed-upon protocols or standardized metrics for assessing their performance, making it difficult to compare findings or cumulatively synthesize evidence across studies. Across 54 recent evaluation studies, we identify ten evaluation dimensions and 40 distinct metrics, operationalized in 96 different ways-35 of them (36%) used by only a single study. Assessment is dominated by documentation efficiency and time, measured in 44 of 54 studies. The other dimensions appear at broadly similar rates (16-24 studies each), and safety and clinical outcome least consistently of all. Ripple effects on the broader care system, such as impact on patients’ care outcomes, redistribution of work, changes in billing and coding intensity, and downstream use of notes by other clinicians are rarely assessed. Moreover, the metrics used rely heavily on self-report and are fragmented and inconsistently operationalized, which limits comparability and hinders synthesis across studies. As an effort to support more rigorous and cumulative evaluation, in this paper we review the study designs, data sources, and metrics commonly used to evaluate ambient AI scribes in healthcare settings, discuss the limitations of current evaluation practice, and argue for a more holistic approach grounded in a standardized, multi-dimensional set of metrics.

Abstract:Children’s peer conflicts increasingly play out in group chats, where tone and timing are stripped away, and a hurtful message is easier to send than to say aloud. In Lilo, the child joins two AI-driven peers mid-argument, coached by a mentor character, also named Lilo, through a Stop-Think-Act traffic light. Through an exploratory study with 28 children (aged 9-11), we examine how children engage with Lilo’s simulated peer conflict and the mentor’s traffic-light interventions. The study included an intervention with Lilo, surveys before and after the intervention, and exit interviews. Participants reported significantly higher self-efficacy for coping with unpleasant messages after their interaction with Lilo. They felt safe experimenting, knowing nothing they wrote would be held against them.

Abstract:This paper presents a descriptive, embedded single-case study examining self-reported AI use within a software organization. The study draws on 98 structured interview records collected across 11 teams, using ten standardized team-level instruments (n = 65) and one instrument with distinct response anchors (n = 33). Among respondents assessed using standardized instruments, 36 of 65 (55.4%) reported AI-use frequency scores of 4 or 5 on a five-point scale. Team-level proportions varied from 20.0% (1/5) to 71.4% (5/7). A record-level cross-tabulation revealed limited awareness or understanding of organizational AI policies across both frequency groups: 86.1% (31/36) of respondents scoring 4-5 and 96.6% (28/29) of those scoring 0-3 reported either no policy awareness or uncertainty about policy details. In the group assessed using the distinct instrument, 31 of 33 respondents (93.9%) scored 4 or 5. Although the pooled proportion reached 68.4% (67/98), differences in response anchors limit direct comparability, making the standardized-instrument results the primary analytical reference. Interviewer-recorded observations provide qualitative context on reported practices and constraints but do not support estimates of their prevalence or causal explanations for differences in AI-use frequency. The findings characterize AI-use patterns and policy awareness within the interviewed sample, without supporting inferences about organization-wide adoption, policy compliance, or the effectiveness of AI use. Abstract:Multimodal datasets that combine synchronised behavioural and physiological signals with subjective affective and body perception measures are still rare. This limits both the understanding of embodied experience and the development of computational models that infer subjective states from sensor data. We introduce BODYinTRANSIT-Lab, a multimodal dataset that addresses this gap by capturing affective, perceptual, and behavioural responses to the Footsteps Illusion. In this closed-loop paradigm, participants perform walking tasks while receiving real-time manipulated auditory feedback of their own footsteps intended to alter perceived body weight. The dataset comprises synchronised recordings from 101 participants recruited through systematic stratification by eating-disorder symptomatology and physical activity level. BODYinTRANSIT-Lab combines full-body kinematics with electromyography, electrocardiography, respiration, and electrodermal activity. Its annotations capture both immediate and post-trial experience, including within-trial perceived-weight ratings, post-trial assessments of body feelings and affective experience, 3D avatar body visualisations, and quantitative body maps. Psychological, behavioural, demographic, and social measures provide further information about factors that may influence individual responses. We provide a deep learning benchmark that uses walking kinematics to classify relative affective valence and perceived weight within subjects. On within-session, segment-level splits, the baseline model achieved mean balanced accuracies of 45.9% for affective valence and 44.5% for perceived weight. The BODYinTRANSIT-Lab dataset provides an experimentally controlled resource for cognitive neuroscience and affective computing research, with potential applications in affect-aware interactive systems, health and well-being technologies, and creative embodied experiences.

[HC-8] From Bias to Positionality: A critical grammar for Large Language Models

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.14079
作者: Dave Murray-Rust,Elisa Giaccardi,Federico Bomba,Maria Luce Lupetti
类目: Computation and Language (cs.CL); Artificial Intelligence (cs.AI); Human-Computer Interaction (cs.HC)
备注:

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Bias has become a default lens for understanding what machine learning systems do and how we should relate to them. Bias is at root a deviation from a standard; in decision making systems we can supply a standard from outside: a law, a protected attribute, a benchmark, a statistical property. However, even there, biased is often used as a shorthand, without stating what the position taken is - a silent ``relative to’‘. In a general use of language models, nothing supplies the standard: there is no decision to audit and no counterfactual output, so the shorthand fails. We argue that positionality – the located, articulated, owned and contestable position from which anything is said – is the better grammar for the question these models now force: who is speaking, from where? Against the vendors’ answer of nowhere and the seductive possibility of everywhere, we argue that when a model is taken as-if speaking, it speaks from somewhere, and this means positionality can describe models, and the way they are believed beyond their warrant, even though they are not accountable speakers. A model’s positionality is laminar – laid down across corpus, tuning, system prompt, application and the live conversation. We separate three sets of factors: the positionality of a model’s creators, the behaviour they intend for it, and the behaviour it enacts, and situate current work within this matrix. This lets us highlight what each stratum inherits from the one below, with ruptures and collapses where that inheritance is disavowed. We then return to where models speak from, and discuss the implications for how models are made, read and held accountable.

Abstract:Extended Reality (XR) technologies can place musicians in virtual, mixed, or real environments during networked music performance (NMP). To examine how NMP applications in XR should be positioned on the reality-virtuality continuum, we conducted a laboratory study (N = 28) comparing a simulated NMP experience in Virtual Reality (VR) with one in Augmented Reality (AR). In both conditions, musicians saw their remote partners in real time as 3D point clouds rendered with an optimized Gaussian Splatting shader. While VR allowed participants to select and customize fully virtual 3D environments, AR showed a pass-through view of the laboratory environment. We measured creativity support, flow, involvement, co-presence, and affect, and complemented these data with qualitative interviews on participants’ preferences and requirements for creative environments. Our results show that participants felt significantly more involved by the immersive XR experience in VR than in AR. Positive affect, flow, and creativity support were strongly correlated in both conditions, whereas involvement correlated with flow and creativity support only in VR. Qualitative findings showed substantial variation in participants’ preferences for AR or VR and also regarding the design of creative virtual environments. Together, these findings suggest that the surrounding environment is a critical design dimension in networked Musical XR, shaping collaborative musical experiences beyond merely representing remote collaborators and mitigating communication latency. Future XR-mediated NMP systems should therefore treat the surrounding space as an integral component of the collaborative musical experience, rather than as a mere visual backdrop. At the same time, they should support experiences across a broad spectrum of the reality-virtuality continuum to accommodate highly individual user requirements.

Abstract: Predicting who will speak next, and when, is a prerequisite for conversational agents and social robots that take turns without waiting for silence. Multiparty next-speaker prediction (NSP) has been studied on corpora with per-speaker sensors, each with its own event definitions. No public benchmark covers the single camera and microphone a robot has, and no model has been compared against how well people perform the same prediction. We turn AVCC, a 31-hour audio-visual corpus of two- and three-speaker online conversation recorded with a single static camera and microphone, into a public NSP benchmark. We add a speaker-disjoint seven-video test partition with 865 hold and 865 shift events at mutual-silence gaps, word-level forced-aligned transcripts for the whole corpus, and a human reference benchmark collected at the same events. We score an audio-only Role-Relative VAP model (RoleVAP) and the multimodal MuVAP model. Labels, transcripts, per-response human data, and the scripts that reproduce every number are released.

Abstract:Mixed-reality (MR) P300 interfaces can register selectable destinations, such as wheelchair goals, directly in the user’s surroundings. When the cues disappear between flashes, however, the user must retain an intended target that is no longer visible. We tested whether such an interface supports target selection and whether giving each cue a stable colour-shape identity improves it compared with visually uniform spheres. Six healthy adults completed four trials in each cue condition of a 5x5 row/column task on a head-mounted MR display, with EEG from Fz, Cz, and Pz. Shrinkage linear discriminant analysis was evaluated with nested validation in which complete trials were held out from class balancing, hyperparameter selection, and fitting. Both conditions evoked a parietal target-related positivity. The decoded cell was correct in 18 of 48 held-out trials, against 1.9 expected by chance (binomial p 1e-12), and in three participants individually. Cue format made no detectable difference: complete-target accuracy was 9/24 in both conditions (paired difference 0.0 percentage points, 95% CI [-37, 37]), and held-out AUC was 0.609 for spheres and 0.585 for object cues. [HC-12] Seeing Without Seeing: A Methodological Review of Visual Mental Imagery Reconstruction from Brain Activity

点击查看摘要

Abstract:Reconstructing visual mental imagery from brain activity differs from reconstructing perceived images. Imagery is generated top-down, its signal is weak, and the imagined content is never observed, so decoders are trained and scored against a proxy such as a cue or a seen exemplar. This criterion-guided methodological review of mainly non-invasive studies (fMRI, EEG, MEG) is narrative rather than systematic. We organise the field into a two-stage pipeline, two design axes and four method families, and formalise target-free evaluation, in which the proxy gap is a systematic bias rather than noise. A two-dimensional admissibility criterion crosses trial-level separability from working-memory maintenance with the memory source of the imagined content. Among the studies reviewed, every image-scored reconstruction concerns a recalled exemplar, none builds a scorable target for concept-generated content, and all come from fMRI, consistent with missing image-level targets in electrophysiological data. Published values for five decoders, compared under a common human forced-choice framing, show seen-to-imagined drops of 5.9 to 26.1 percentage points and a change in method ordering. We treat this as a diagnostic signal, not a controlled benchmark result, and specify a within-subject test for an altered neural code. Beyond this synthesis, we make two proposals. First, because frozen generative priors can produce photorealistic images weakly tied to neural signals, we combine existing null-signal controls into a normalised neural dependence with a within-category null, an unvalidated diagnostic quantity. Second, we propose a candidate ten-item reporting checklist with illustrative pass criteria. In an exploratory application to ten studies, none reports all items in a fully checkable form; this describes reporting practice, not study quality.

[HC-13] A computational framework for understanding embodied plans

链接: https://arxiv.org/abs/2611.13669
作者: Aalap D. Shah,Basil Saeed,Joshua B. Tenenbaum,Tobias Gerstenberg,Hyowon Gweon,Ilker Yildirim

Abstract:Reasoning about people’s plans and goals based on their actions is fundamental to human social interaction and essential for cooperative, embodied artificial intelligence. Formalizing this capacity in naturalistic, embodied settings has been a longstanding challenge. Here, we present GenEA, a novel agent representation capable of reasoning over multi-step, long-horizon embodied plans. At the heart of GenEA lies a multilevel state-space that couples the coarse biomechanics of an articulated body and its interactions with nearby objects by extending the task-and-motion planning framework from robotics with simulation-based intuitive physics. By embedding this state-space in a generative model, GenEA yields a joint probability distribution over goals and embodied plans. Across several experiments spanning the qualitatively distinct domains of object manipulation and navigation, featuring diverse tasks and multiple behavioral measures, we show that GenEA, through simple transformations of this joint distribution, recapitulates how humans reason about embodied plans. Crucially, GenEA consistently outperforms strong alternative models, including plausible heuristics, standard task-and-motion planning, and a state-of-the-art vision-language model. GenEA thereby offers a new perspective on the architecture of human reasoning and social cognition, suggesting that embodied artificial intelligence systems seeking to seamlessly interact with humans should adopt GenEA-like generative models of action planning.

Abstract:Benchmarking is a valuable technique for advancing the capabilities of Large Language Models (LLMs), including in personal health informatics. However, it is unclear whether and how well these efforts align with needs and considerations of personal health informatics process. Addressing this need, we first analyzed 53,587 tasks across eight benchmarks related to personal health informatics and characterized the space of benchmark design. We then contrasted our observations of design choices with personal informatics theories and empirical knowledge. We find significant mismatches between existing benchmark design and domain guidelines and understanding. This lack of alignment limits the utility of the evidence current benchmarks offer about LLM capabilities. We use domain knowledge to highlight capabilities benchmarks should include and discuss opportunities our work enables for taking a human-centered and domain-driven approach to benchmark design.

Abstract:What if a single face-facing camera could sense your surroundings—through your eyes? We introduce EyeQ, which explores corneal reflection as a modality for context-aware mobile interaction. Traditional vision-based context sensing relies on world-facing cameras that demand explicit aiming or dual-camera setups; EyeQ instead shows that an off-the-shelf VLM can read scene context from corneal reflections captured with a smartphone camera. To recover usable detail from mobile corneal crops, EyeQ pairs on-device iris-guided capture with server-side AI enhancement, then leverages VLMs to extract scene types, names, and objects from warped, unfamiliar eye-image sequences. In an N=10 study, we characterize how capture conditions shape reflection fidelity, evaluate what VLMs detect, misclassify, and hallucinate, and demonstrate interaction opportunities, including detecting a steering wheel to distinguish drivers from passengers. This work reframes the eye in HCI—from a target for gaze estimation to a passive mirror of one’s surroundings—and examines the privacy tensions it raises.

Abstract:Musical AI systems behave in non-linear, dynamic ways that exceed the tool-oriented framings inherited from earlier instrument design. Existing frames of control and ensemble interaction do not articulate the entangled, relational agency that emerges when performers work with AI feedback instruments over time. We examine a duet practice with two AI-enabled feedback instruments, Sù and Agentier, in which feedback operates at the inner level of the AI’s recurrent processes and the outer loop of musical interaction between performer, instrument, and co-performer. Our work draws on agential realism and a diffractive dialogue methodology to read our independent reflections through one another across five performances, examining how agency is enacted between performers and AI instruments. We find that control and agency are relational and shift across performances; musical textures enact feedback moments of control with performers; reaching a productive feedback environment is itself a shared exploratory act; and performers maintain their instruments through funnelling and injection, developing the skill of navigating agency along a continuous spectrum. Feedback musicianship with AI instruments demands navigation of this relational agency, displacing the leading-versus-responding binary that initially framed our reflections. This work contributes a materially-grounded vocabulary for AI feedback musicianship and a model of human-AI creative collaboration in which mutual agency is worked for through practice rather than designed in.

Abstract:Designing effective instruction requires instructional designers to create assessment questions aligned with clearly defined knowledge components (KCs). These KCs represent specific knowledge or skills that students must acquire. This process is often time-consuming and relies heavily on expert labor. Although AI for education research has produced a growing body of automated question-generation and KC-discovery methods, few have moved beyond research prototypes into user-friendly tools that instructional designers can readily use. To bridge the research-to-practice gap, we developed and evaluated an educational intelligence platform that unifies question generation and KC discovery behind a single interface to support instructional content development. Named “Perspicacious,” our platform aims to help instructional designers “see through” complex data and algorithms to derive instructional insights. A cost model calibrated on 17 production runs revealed a cost-time trade-off: extracting KCs from a 576-question bank cost US 1.98-4.11 and took 36-158 minutes to complete, depending on the budget. A formative, partially Wizard-of-Oz study with eight instructional designers found strong perceived usability (mean SUS 78.8) and surfaced concrete requirements that we treat as prerequisites for deployment.

Abstract:Recent work in human-computer interaction and allied fields has sought to engage community members as co-designers, facilitators, and decision makers to challenge structural power barriers and knowledge gaps. In this paper, we apply a diverse set of computational techniques to engage and address community concerns surrounding the socio-environmental impacts of the Greenidge Bitcoin mining power plant facility in upstate New York. Through collaborative interactions with community groups, addressing problems ranging from regulatory inertia to thermal water pollution, we aim to facilitate not just the production of new and critical environmental knowledge but also new computationally-supported repertoires of contention: means of contesting the unequal relations of knowledge and power that structure and often determine the outcomes of environmental controversies.
